Asset quality is the strong leg (GNPA 2.37%, NNPA 0.60%, PCR above 90.5%, gross slippages below 0.5%, credit cost 0.1%) and the P&L hit is mix/one-off rather than credit. The whole thesis now rests on a **Q2 FY27 self-correction** management has explicitly promised — bulk deposits shed "starting this month itself", technically-written-off recoveries that slipped out of Q1 landing in Q2, and ROA back to 1.25%+ "from quarter 2 itself" — with guidance deliberately left unchanged until the Q2 print.

Two-sided cause, as management framed it: (a) yield on advances fell to **8.56%** from **9.35%** CPLY — industry-wide, "nearly two-thirds of all bank credit in India now carries an interest rate below 9% compared to around 44% a year earlier, as per RBI data"; (b) rate-cut transmission on the deposit side has been limited, so cost of deposits moderated only **9 bps** to **4.74%**.
- **The margin hit was a choice, not a slip.** MD: "we had to depend on the credit opportunities that were available in rest of India… the good corporates are competitive in nature… For that, we had to raise deposits… we had to raise some deposits at certainly — a certain bit of high costs. So this is a decision which was taken for this quarter to ensure that the growth momentum was kept up." And: "**it is an aberration for 1 quarter only.**"
- **Analyst pushback was sharp and unresolved on the numbers** — "a 5% sequential growth in the loan book in 1 quarter can shave off about 20 basis points of margins. Then I'm just trying to understand the rationale behind this sort of opportunistic choice?" MD conceded the pricing point without quantifying: "we intend to reduce it, the proportion — reduce that proportion to a more realistic level, which was a little bit too high in the last financial year and in the first quarter of this year."
- **Recovery mechanics management committed to:** bulk deposits (~INR 6,700 cr of the quarter's growth) "will be **shed in the coming months, starting this month itself**" and "It will come down in a month or 2"; low-yield legacy loans mature "this month and next month"; retail yields run "**at least 200 basis points**" above corporate. An analyst summarised the bridge back to 3.5% and MD replied: "I could not have explained it in a better way than what you did."
- **Opex** — cost ratio improving "for… last 6, 7 quarters"; guided flat-to-better, with recruitment the only upward pressure. Q1's ~INR 650 cr employee cost is the FY27 base (Q4 FY26's INR 509 cr was reversal-flattered); this quarter carries the annual provisioning for pre-2008/2009 non-NPS staff, of which gratuity + pension + leave ≈ **INR 150 crores**.

non-obvious takeaways:
- **The PAT decline is a provisioning *sign-flip*, not credit deterioration.** CPLY had ~3% advances *degrowth* → standard-asset provision **reversal** (a P&L credit); this quarter's 25% growth → standard-asset provision **charge**. Bad-debt provisions actually fell and credit cost is 0.1%. The YoY PAT comparison is therefore close to meaningless without adjusting both legs.
- **Three of the four ugly QoQ optics are prior-quarter distortions, not this quarter's deterioration** — cost of deposits (INR 105 cr Laadli Beti), employee cost (terminal-benefit reversal), retail segment profit (TWO recoveries parked in retail). Q4 FY26 was the flattered quarter.
- **Management is guiding 12% while expecting 18–20%** and said so on the same call — the guidance is deliberately a floor, and the bank has now been told by investors that this is a problem. Anyone modelling off the stated guide is modelling off a number management has already disowned.
- **The savings→term-deposit shift management blames on industry financialization is, in its own case, mostly one government payout.** The macro framing is real (SCB term-deposit share 58%→61% FY19→FY26; equity+MF share of financial savings 27%→46% FY20→FY25), but the bank's *own* CASA decline traces to J&K state terminal-benefit disbursements landing in savings in Q4 and rolling into its own 888-day product in Q1.
- **A "regional bank" is quietly repricing itself as a national one** — ROI from <20% to ~26% of business in a year, 22 states, 50–70 new branches planned, ~300 hires, and an explicit statement of intent to be "considered as one of the national banks." The margin damage this quarter is the entry cost of that transition.
- **Market-cap/ATH milestone is a post-quarter event** (10 July 2026, mcap > INR 20,000 cr) and institutional holding rose 11.5%→15.74% Y-o-Y — i.e. the re-rating happened *before* this margin-miss print landed.

hero.oneLiner: A deliberate "growth-over-margin" quarter that management itself calls **"an aberration for 1 quarter only"**: J&KBANK crossed **INR 3 trillion of business** with advances **+25.44% Y-o-Y** and deposits **+16.75% Y-o-Y** (its first sequential Q1 deposit growth in 6 years), but funded that with ~**INR 6,700 crores of higher-cost bulk deposits** to chase competitively-priced Rest-of-India corporate credit — so **NIM compressed to 3.28%** against a 3.5% full-year guide, and **net profit fell to INR 424 crores** even as operating profit rose 5% to INR 703 crores. Asset quality is the strong leg (GNPA 2.37%, NNPA 0.60%, PCR above 90.5%, gross slippages below 0.5%, credit cost 0.1%) and the P&L hit is mix/one-off rather than credit. The whole thesis now rests on a **Q2 FY27 self-correction** management has explicitly promised — bulk deposits shed "starting this month itself", technically-written-off recoveries that slipped out of Q1 landing in Q2, and ROA back to 1.25%+ "from quarter 2 itself" — with guidance deliberately left unchanged until the Q2 print.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Geography.** J&K + Ladakh remains the core (61.13% banking-business market share as on 31-Mar-2026); Rest of India now ~26% of business vs <20% a year ago, present "across 22 states". Deposits are **83% from J&K** while advances are **62% in J&K** *(analyst-stated)* — i.e. the home franchise funds ROI lending. MD on balancing this: "The composition of deposits, advances… we expect it to balance out in the **next 2 to 3 years**."
- **RAM.** Retail + Agri + MSME ≈ "around two-thirds of our loan book". Agriculture advances **+~18% Y-o-Y**. Retail advances "registered a double-digit Y-o-Y growth". ROI personal loans **+12%+**; **car loans the best performer — +20%+ bank level, +30%+ in ROI**; ROI housing and education loans double-digit. J&K retail volumes: "the retail growth has **doubled** this year first quarter" vs Q1 last year; retail + agri together "almost 20% to 30% improvement over last year's growth."
- **Corporate / Financial Markets.** Corporate credit outpaced retail this quarter — "higher bond yields have pushed companies back to the banking system" plus "a conscious preference for selective lending to well-rated corporates." The financial-markets segment's sharp growth is **not** short-term credit: "for the last 12 months or so, we have stayed away from short-term lending… mostly **repo linked**" (explicitly *not* MCLR, *not* T-bill). Concentration: "It is diversified. It is diversified. It is totally diversified."
- **Deposits.** Term deposits +24%+ Y-o-Y vs CASA +~7.5%. The savings→term migration is largely mechanical: Q4 FY26 saw the state government release "quite a substantial amount of terminal benefits of retired employees" into savings accounts, which "subsequently, in the first quarter… got converted into term deposits", chiefly into the bank's own **888-day deposit scheme** (rate raised **5 bps** in the last 1–2 months). A **GM-headed vertical exclusively for CASA** has been created.
- **Associate — PNB MetLife.** "we have also entered into a transaction to sell our stake into MetLife" (analyst framing) → one-off gain expected; MD: "we are waiting for… a few clearances to come across and then we will — **we have not yet decided how to go about it**" (including whether to route it into an ECL buffer).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
**FY 2026-27 guidance kept UNCHANGED, verbatim:** *"We would like to keep the guidance for financial year 2026-27 unchanged for now and we will reassess the same only after the quarter 2 results. Credit growth, 12% deposit growth, 10%, CASA 45% NIM around 3.5%, ROA maintaining around 2026 levels, ROE around 16%, GNPA below 2.25%."*

> ⚠️ **Transcript punctuation is ambiguous** in that sentence (no separators between metric/value pairs). The natural reading is credit growth **12%**, deposit growth **10%**, CASA **45%**, NIM **~3.5%**, ROA ~FY26 levels, ROE **~16%**, GNPA **below 2.25%**. The credit-growth = 12% leg is independently corroborated later by an analyst restatement management accepted: *"we have been guiding for about 12% growth… For FY27, again, we are guiding for 12% technically."* The other pairings are **not** separately corroborated on the call — treat as a reading, not a quote.

Management's own expectation, stated as running **ahead** of that guidance:
- **Credit growth:** "although the guidance given is around 12%, but the actual credit growth will not be less than, say, **18% to 20%**, I expect." Split: J&K **12–13%**, Rest of India **~25%**.
- **Mix shift:** "I expect almost **55% to 60%** growth of advances coming this year from retail itself"; "I expect the retail growth to be slightly more than the corporate growth by the end of this year." ROI retail "going at an improvement of 30% is likely to improve to around 100% because the base is low."
- **NIM:** "I believe we will be around **3.5% very soon, if not by the end of this quarter, maybe by the end of the third quarter, definitely.**" Driver: retail yields "at least **200 basis points** more than the yields that we have had in the corporate loan book" + bulk-deposit shedding.
- **ROA:** "**1.25% plus.** In fact, it should be somewhere around what it was last year." Timing: "It should be **from quarter 2 itself**."
- **CASA:** "I'm very hopeful that we will be able to improve the CASA by the **end of third quarter** this year substantially."
- **Opex:** "at worst, it will be flat. It will continue to improve… there won't be any increase" — the only upside risk being the planned recruitment. Employee cost: "the employee cost for this quarter should be a base and it is likely to come down slightly from there till we have the next round of recruitment."
- **Technically-written-off recoveries:** "expected recovery is almost **INR250 crores**… It can be somewhere around **INR300 crores**", and "I expect the written off recovery to continue for at least **1 more year. That is '27, '28 as well.**"
- **FY27 PAT vs FY26:** asked whether FY26's INR 2,367 crores *(analyst-stated)* would be exceeded — "No, no, obviously, we are going to exceed it."
- **ECL:** prior quantification of INR 1,600–1,700 crores net-worth impact reiterated as broadly unchanged — "I don't see much of a change as to the numbers you have mentioned… according to me, it should be **slightly lesser** than that."
- **Branches:** "Jammu and Kashmir, we tend to increase around **15 to 20 branches every year**. But we intend to increase **50 to 70 branches in rest of India in the next 2 years**."

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Rest-of-India retail build-out** — "we have posted **100-odd people**, and we are **recruiting around 300 people in rest of India**"; ROI retail growth expected to go from ~30% to "around 100% because the base is low"; 50–70 new ROI branches over 2 years. Explicit national ambition: "we would definitely want to be considered as one of the national banks. So we do not want to confine ourselves as a regional bank."
- **CASA franchise re-take in home geography** — salary-package MOUs (J&K Police, J&K government 5-year renewal, 3 corporate MOUs in July, Bangalore schools) + transaction-banking initiatives; deposit market share already regained in 19 of 22 districts.
- **Written-off recovery annuity** — ~INR 250–300 cr/yr expected to persist through FY27 **and** FY28, against an already ~90.5%+ covered book.
- **Tourism/economic normalisation in J&K** — "economic activity having already picked up in Jammu and Kashmir as **tourism has returned to normal**", after a year when "we did not have a conducive business environment because of all that had happened."
- **PNB MetLife stake monetisation** — undeployed one-off gain, optionally an ECL buffer.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **NIM 3.28%**, compressed. Two-sided cause, as management framed it: (a) yield on advances fell to **8.56%** from **9.35%** CPLY — industry-wide, "nearly two-thirds of all bank credit in India now carries an interest rate below 9% compared to around 44% a year earlier, as per RBI data"; (b) rate-cut transmission on the deposit side has been limited, so cost of deposits moderated only **9 bps** to **4.74%**.
- **The margin hit was a choice, not a slip.** MD: "we had to depend on the credit opportunities that were available in rest of India… the good corporates are competitive in nature… For that, we had to raise deposits… we had to raise some deposits at certainly — a certain bit of high costs. So this is a decision which was taken for this quarter to ensure that the growth momentum was kept up." And: "**it is an aberration for 1 quarter only.**"
- **Analyst pushback was sharp and unresolved on the numbers** — "a 5% sequential growth in the loan book in 1 quarter can shave off about 20 basis points of margins. Then I'm just trying to understand the rationale behind this sort of opportunistic choice?" MD conceded the pricing point without quantifying: "we intend to reduce it, the proportion — reduce that proportion to a more realistic level, which was a little bit too high in the last financial year and in the first quarter of this year."
- **Recovery mechanics management committed to:** bulk deposits (~INR 6,700 cr of the quarter's growth) "will be **shed in the coming months, starting this month itself**" and "It will come down in a month or 2"; low-yield legacy loans mature "this month and next month"; retail yields run "**at least 200 basis points**" above corporate. An analyst summarised the bridge back to 3.5% and MD replied: "I could not have explained it in a better way than what you did."
- **Opex** — cost ratio improving "for… last 6, 7 quarters"; guided flat-to-better, with recruitment the only upward pressure. Q1's ~INR 650 cr employee cost is the FY27 base (Q4 FY26's INR 509 cr was reversal-flattered); this quarter carries the annual provisioning for pre-2008/2009 non-NPS staff, of which gratuity + pension + leave ≈ **INR 150 crores**.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **CAR 16.67%, CET1 13.91%** as on 30 June 2026 — "The Bank continues to build upon its capital buffers."
- **Capital raise:** "Capital raise, **INR1,250 crores** is already done that is approved and that is going to come, but we are **thinking in terms of revising the quantum**. I'm not in a position to divulge more because we are still waiting for the approvals." Confirmed as an upward revision requiring fresh approval; on whether the government participates or holds its stake: "**They might dilute.**" MD also framed the raise as ECL-preparation: "we may be — this year itself, we may be going to the market to raise funds capital. So I think we are, at the moment, sufficiently well placed to manage the ECL impact."
- **ECL transition:** INR 1,600–1,700 crores net-worth impact previously quantified, reiterated as "slightly lesser than that"; final view deferred — "Once the ECL model is finalized, I will be in a better position to say."
- **PNB MetLife sale proceeds:** use undecided; ECL-buffer route floated by an analyst and left open ("Maybe we can take your idea as well").
- No dividend / buyback discussion on this call.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
- MD Amitava Chatterjee is unusually candid about the trade-off he made, and pre-empts the criticism in his opening remarks: "this quarterly performance should be viewed in entirety… rather than just through the prism of short-term profitability. The choices and decisions that we have made during this quarter have been **conscious, strategic and forward-looking**."
- He accepts the guidance-divergence criticism without deflection, and takes an analyst's suggestion on the MetLife proceeds ("Maybe we can take your idea as well") — a constructive tone.
- But the confidence is at times untethered from disclosure: "next quarter, you just wait. I mean, if you have that patience, you wait and see the ROA next quarter"; "I'm absolutely certain about that"; "No, no, obviously, we are going to exceed it" on FY27 PAT. **No hard numeric bridge from 3.28% to 3.5% NIM was provided** despite three separate analysts pressing on margins — the answers were directional (retail +200 bps yield, bulk shed) rather than quantified.
- Data handling on the call was slightly loose: the bulk-deposit number needed a pause to retrieve, and the pension provisioning figure was stated as INR 130 crores then corrected by a colleague to "INR150 crores total gratuity pension and leave."

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Home-market share that is close to structural** — "a commanding market share of **61.13%** of banking business as on 31st March 2026" in J&K and Ladakh, plus deposit-share **improvement in 19 out of 22 districts** during FY 2025-26. Crucially, the ROI diversification "has been achieved **without compromising** on our market leadership in our home territories."
- **Deposit-cost moat / funding franchise** — 83% of deposits are raised in J&K *(analyst-stated)* and lent partly outside; cost of deposits **4.74%** is the enabler of the ROI corporate push. MD names it as the reason the sector's #1 problem is survivable: "the only challenge that the entire industry is facing is what we are also facing is that of deposit growth. So **fortunately, we have been able to counter that because we have a very strong deposit franchise in this geography.**"
- **88-year incumbency / local underwriting knowledge** — answering whether ROI expansion means weaker customer understanding: "this bank has been operating in Jammu and Kashmir for 88 years. So I don't think **any other bank or any other institution understands the pulse of Jammu and Kashmir better than J&K Bank**." Corroborated by the numbers rather than asserted alone: gross slippages below 0.5%, credit cost 0.1%, SMA declining.
- **Government/institutional account capture** — the J&K government salary MOU (5-year renewal in process) and J&K Police salary-account MOU are a captive-float advantage a non-local competitor cannot easily replicate.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Guidance credibility is now an explicit investor grievance.** "last guidance that we had in the month of May didn't really indicate anything of what has gotten delivered in the first quarter… I would really appreciate if the delivery is not so divergent or maybe if we could guide slightly more closer to what the delivery would be." MD: "Sure, Umang, Sure." Guiding 12% credit growth while expecting 18–20% is the live example. **Watch whether the Q2 reassessment closes this gap.**
- **The entire margin thesis is back-ended into Q2/Q3** — bulk-deposit shedding, low-yield loan runoff, retail mix-shift and the TWO recovery all have to land. If Q2 does not normalise, the FY27 ROA 1.25%/NIM 3.5%/ROE 16% frame breaks together.
- **Funding concentration / structural mismatch** — 83% of deposits from J&K funding 38% of advances outside it *(analyst-stated)*; management's own fix is a 2–3 year project.
- **CASA erosion is structural, not only seasonal.** CASA 42.06% against a 45% guide, with savings migrating into the bank's own 888-day term product; management's counter (decade-long Q1 pattern) explains the *seasonality* but not the mix drift.
- **ECL transition** — INR 1,600–1,700 cr net-worth impact, model not yet finalised, capital raise quantum still unapproved.
- **Deposit growth is the named industry-wide risk** — "The only challenge, if I have to mention that, only challenge that the entire industry is facing… is that of deposit growth."
- **Geopolitics / macro** — IMF trimmed India's FY2026 GDP forecast by 10 bps to 6.4%; "breakdown of diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East." Bank's own outlook hinges on "hopeful that the geopolitical tensions will also ease."
- **J&K floods** — probed by an analyst; MD says immaterial so far: "the impact has not been that much. So at the moment, nothing is visible, which I can say will impact collections. Collections have been proper." **Verify next quarter** — this call was 29 July 2026.
- **IT-sector employment stress → housing/unsecured risk** — MD sees none, with a specific reason: "our exposure to the employees of the IT sector is quite **low**."
- **Government shareholder may dilute** in the enlarged raise.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The PAT decline is a provisioning *sign-flip*, not credit deterioration.** CPLY had ~3% advances *degrowth* → standard-asset provision **reversal** (a P&L credit); this quarter's 25% growth → standard-asset provision **charge**. Bad-debt provisions actually fell and credit cost is 0.1%. The YoY PAT comparison is therefore close to meaningless without adjusting both legs.
- **Three of the four ugly QoQ optics are prior-quarter distortions, not this quarter's deterioration** — cost of deposits (INR 105 cr Laadli Beti), employee cost (terminal-benefit reversal), retail segment profit (TWO recoveries parked in retail). Q4 FY26 was the flattered quarter.
- **Management is guiding 12% while expecting 18–20%** and said so on the same call — the guidance is deliberately a floor, and the bank has now been told by investors that this is a problem. Anyone modelling off the stated guide is modelling off a number management has already disowned.
- **The savings→term-deposit shift management blames on industry financialization is, in its own case, mostly one government payout.** The macro framing is real (SCB term-deposit share 58%→61% FY19→FY26; equity+MF share of financial savings 27%→46% FY20→FY25), but the bank's *own* CASA decline traces to J&K state terminal-benefit disbursements landing in savings in Q4 and rolling into its own 888-day product in Q1.
- **A "regional bank" is quietly repricing itself as a national one** — ROI from <20% to ~26% of business in a year, 22 states, 50–70 new branches planned, ~300 hires, and an explicit statement of intent to be "considered as one of the national banks." The margin damage this quarter is the entry cost of that transition.
- **Market-cap/ATH milestone is a post-quarter event** (10 July 2026, mcap > INR 20,000 cr) and institutional holding rose 11.5%→15.74% Y-o-Y — i.e. the re-rating happened *before* this margin-miss print landed.
